The investigation traced the flow of INR 4,70,000 originating from seed wallet 0xa7f39c1d8e4b2a5f7c3d9e0a1b8c6d4e5f2a67e9 on 8 September 2026 at 10:31 IST. Within three hops, the funds were dispersed through 17 transfers involving 14 distinct blockchain entities, of which 16 transfers were confirmed and one inferred. The movement displayed rapid automated dispersal, with the first outbound transaction occurring three minutes after receipt, interaction with a mixer contract (transfer of 1,500 USDT to 0x8589f2c47b1d0a63e95482f7ca1b3d6e0f4a0b6f), and subsequent exposure to a cross‑chain bridge (0xbb17d4a09e26c35f81b0d7a94e13c68f05b2c530) within two downstream hops. Sixteen of the transfers met or exceeded the 30 % reporting threshold, indicating a high‑volume redistribution pattern.

Risk scoring assigned a HIGH rating (65/100) to the seed wallet, elevated by proximity to a known scam cluster (+20), rapid automated dispersal (+15), mixer interaction (+15), and bridge exposure (+15). The highest‑scoring entity observed was 0x9c04a7e3b21d5f86c0a94e7d2b83f150c6ead21e with a CRITICAL score of 75/100, followed by the seed wallet (HIGH) and 0x3f1a7d92c04e8b56af10d3e7b829c45d6e0a71bc (MEDIUM).
